quote: I would add a backing-up and run-up maneuver
say: Astra says the fix is a run-up: back away from the ramp first, then come back fast.

check.note: The car reverses for 13 steps, reaches x = 4.31, then returns at 3.67 sideways, the same speed as Claude run 3.

quote: Leftward acceleration continues until approximately x = 2.25, provided leftward speed exceeds 2.5.
say: Astra keeps the throttle on through the ramp, but only while the car is moving left faster than 2.5.

check.note: The foot of the ramp cuts sideways speed from 2.74 to 2.17 at step 57 (x = 2.30). That is under the 2.5 condition, so the rule stops driving left before the jump.

quote: A slow approach can trigger another run-up
say: If the car comes in too slowly, the rule starts over and backs up again.

check.note: The rule fired as written, but it fired mid-jump. Reverse held from step 57 until green touched red at step 68, with no second run-up.

quote: This is a physics-based, untested patch—not a measured success-rate claim.
say: Astra says plainly that it has not tested the edit.

check.note: The result was 0 of 1,024. Its episode matches Claude run 3 to within 0.001 through step 57, when this rule reversed and Claude’s stayed on throttle.
